missing_details: Definition of a cellular automaton on a group G, including the state space S^G endowed with the prodiscrete (product) topology
Requirement that the transition function f: S^G → S^G be continuous
Requirement that f be G-equivariant (commute with the group action)
Quantification over all finite alphabets S
Formal definitions of injective and surjective functions in this context
refined_question: Does every group G have the property that for every finite set S, any function f: S^G → S^G which is continuous (with respect to the prodiscrete topology on S^G), G-equivariant, and injective is necessarily surjective?
equivalent_formulation: A group G is surjunctive if for every finite set S, every continuous, G-equivariant, injective function f: S^G → S^G is also surjective.
justification: The original problem name identifies only that one must determine if all groups lie in the class of surjunctive groups, but does not define the technical terms or specify the quantifiers required to make the question precise. The refined question incorporates all necessary definitions: the domain S^G with the prodiscrete topology, the continuity and G-equivariance conditions on the transition function, the injectivity-to-surjectivity implication, and the universal quantification over finite alphabets S, directly following the canonical formulation in the Definition section. The equivalence is taken verbatim from the article’s statement of an equivalent characterization.
